source.title: Mean field theory for deep dropout networks: digging up gradient backpropagation deeply
source.authors: Wei Huang; R. Xu; Wei-Tao Du; Yutian Zeng; Yun-Ce Zhao

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplemental material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies training outcomes across depth and initialization settings using training-accuracy heatmaps, a different measure from the versions’ explicit near-zero-error claims.
record.gate_note: Figure 7 reports training accuracy across depth and initial weight variance for eight training recipes. The text describes the heatmaps and compares trainable-length predictions; cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 7 directly repeats and extends the initialization-versus-depth training experiments of Deep Information Propagation, including matched optimizers and learning rates. These results test V4's trainable-depth component. Fully connected networks do not test V1's convolutional-network claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's trainable-length paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose L≤min{12ξ1,12ξ2} for networks with and without dropout, reducing to 12ξ1 without dropout. Their broader conclusions also include conjectured shared χ1 scaling of single-input and paired-input gradients and a universal squared-mean relationship for gradient variance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fully connected dropout networks and training-accuracy heatmaps across depth and initial weight variance; the claim versions include other architectures and outcomes such as classification error or training speed.
record.method_sensitivity: Trainability depends on depth and initial weight variance; the paper also varies dataset, optimizer, dropout rate, and initialization across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed 6ξ2 trainability boundary underestimates the trainable region, while 12ξ2 overestimates its right boundary in the reported no-dropout comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maximum trainable depth is empirically better described by min{12ξ1,12ξ2} than by 6ξ2 in these experiments. This refines a quantitative prediction that V4 does not state.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 reports τ=f1(ηL) without dropout and τ=f2(η) with dropout up to L=120 at keep rate 0.99 and L=55 at 0.98.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At χ1=1, depth and dropout alter learning-rate scaling for steps to 25% test accuracy. This does not compare initialization choices or measure a stability threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization-only simulations suggest that single-input and paired-input gradient metrics share χ1 scaling, and their variances scale approximately as squared means.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient statistics in random dropout networks follow shared propagation and variance-scaling laws; these measurements alone do not establish training speed or successful optimization.

record.problems: Figure 7 heatmap values are not numerically reported in the text; precise training accuracies and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The heatmaps concern fully connected networks and do not establish near-zero training error in the text.

untested.parts: The convolutional-network claim, including near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, label corruption, and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated special-initialization alternatives.

Activation-matched initialization comparisons; faster learning from orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian weights in very deep tanh networks; orthogonal convolution kernels and 10000-layer training. Figure 7's activation is not specified in the supplied text.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup alternatives.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is warranted. Unreadable exact heatmap accuracies do not imply a partial effect: the supplied text explicitly describes the V4 trainability boundaries. The quantitative correction to an original source's depth-scale formula does not itself challenge V4's broader wording.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fully connected networks on MNIST and CIFAR10; does not test convolutional networks, CIFAR100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or the stated regularized recipes. Training accuracy is shown, without an explicit near-zero training-error result.

Tests Gaussian and orthogonal weight initialization in fully connected networks, including depth-dependent training outcomes. Does not test activation-matched initialization, tanh networks, or orthogonal convolution kernels at 10,000 layers.
